bullets: Last game (7 of 7) of the session video; only the final ~102 s were readable, starting mid-game at roughly clock 1:55 in double elixir with Ryley already ahead (his towers 4781/4858, the enemy left tower 3686). Ryley names the list himself at t=1285: "a 98% win rate with with 2.0 log bait cycle" — Skeletons, Ice Spirit, Electro Spirit, Wall Breakers, Berserker, Cannon, Dart Goblin, Goblin Barrel, exactly 16 elixir, with Evo Dart Goblin in play.

The deck's defensive answer to an Evolution Royal Giant in this game is not the Cannon but chip plus a refusal to trade: Evo Dart Goblin at [9, 9] at clock 1:31 "just to start getting some damage on the RG", then at clock 1:25 "I'm not even going to go for the cannon. I'm just going to let this go because even though we take some damage here, I think it's more beneficial to eat this damage and just go in" — he pays 490 tower HP to keep his elixir on offence.

Offence is Wall Breakers volume in one lane rather than a built push: sets at clock 1:45 [3, 14], 1:17 [4, 15], 1:05 and 0:59 [3, 14], with a Goblin Barrel at [3, 25] at clock 1:22 in between. The enemy left tower goes 3086 -> 895 HP across clock 1:15-0:57. He states the bait logic outright — "Maybe we force out the bats, but even if I don't, I don't really care" (1237-1240).

Cycle speed is used to time throws off the opponent's rotation, not off his own bar: "He used his bomber, so he's not back to the bomber yet" (clock 0:57) and "That's going to be a full barrel on the tower. He has no elixir" (clock 1:03).

The 1-elixir cards do three separate jobs in one game: Ice Spirit as the cheap freeze on an incoming Bomber (clock 1:47, [8, 9]), Electro Spirit as the named Bats answer (clock 1:05), Skeletons as pure cycle and as a hold-the-lead placement behind his own tower at clock 0:48 ("Now we just have to defend for another 48 seconds").

Result: win. From clock 0:48 the opponent stops answering ("he gave up. He's not playing anything", t=1266) and a Dart Goblin / Berserker / Wall Breakers / Skeletons / Ice Spirit push on the right takes that tower from ~4499 to 128 HP before the capture ends on the results screen — "Let's go. Dude, very nice win, guys".

new_deck.rationale: Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel are the win conditions and every support card (Dart Goblin, Skeletons, the two spirits) is a small-spell bait, while the 2.0 average elixir means the whole deck is a cycle shell around them.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: At exactly 2.0 average elixir the deck cycles back to Wall Breakers and Goblin Barrel faster than a mid-ladder deck can rotate its answers, which is how Ryley wins this game: five Wall Breakers sets and two Barrels into one lane while the opponent is still paying six elixir for a Royal Giant. The bait layer is real — Dart Goblin, Goblin Barrel, Skeletons and the spirits all pull the same small spell, so he can say "maybe we force out the bats, but even if I don't, I don't really care" and be right either way. Cannon is the only true defensive card, and this match shows he treats it as optional: with a tower lead he lets an Evolution Royal Giant hit rather than spend three elixir off the cycle. The two 1-elixir spirits split the defensive work (Ice Spirit freeze for ground pushes, Electro Spirit for Bats and other swarms) so the Dart Goblin can be used offensively for tank chip instead of being the only answer. The obvious cost is that the deck has no reset for a big tank if it falls behind — every plan in this game depends on already being ahead on towers.
